life_history: Mr. Johnson is a truck driver who was recently diagnosed with high cholesterol. He presented to a pharmacist with significant hesitation regarding his newly prescribed cholesterol-lowering medication. His occupational demands involve heavy physical labor, specifically hauling heavy boxes on a dolly. The precipitant to his reluctance is the doctor's warning about muscle weakness as a potential side effect, which threatens his current livelihood. He is married and highly motivated by his plan to retire in 4 to 5 years and travel actively to places like the Fjords in Norway.
intermediate_beliefs: Positive assumption: If I avoid taking the cholesterol medication, then I can protect my muscle strength and keep working; negative assumption: If I take the medication, then I will develop muscle weakness, lose my livelihood as a truck driver, and be unable to support myself.
intermediate_beliefs_during_depression: If my health declines or I develop unmanageable side effects, it proves I have no control over my body and my dreams of an active retirement will be permanently ruined.
coping_strategies: Maladaptive coping includes treatment avoidance (initially intending to refuse prescribed medication due to fear of occupational impairment). Adaptive coping includes openly discussing his side-effect concerns with the pharmacist, engaging in psychoeducation to evaluate long-term health risks versus short-term side effects, and committing to future dietary lifestyle changes to further manage his cholesterol.

cognitive_models.situation: The doctor prescribes cholesterol medication and warns about potential muscle weakness as a side effect.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: I'm not so certain I'm even gonna take the medicine. I'm a truck driver and I got a haul heavy boxes out of the truck on a dolly. I can't afford muscle weakness right now.
cognitive_models.behavior: Opposing taking the medicine and expressing treatment reluctance to the pharmacist.

cognitive_models.situation: The pharmacist prompts him to discuss the long-term elevated risks of untreated high cholesterol, specifically stroke and heart attack.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: Having a stroke or a heart attack would really be bad. My wife and I want to retire in four to five years and visit The Fjords, Norway. We want to live our dreams actively.
cognitive_models.behavior: Engaging in change talk and acknowledging the severity of leaving the condition untreated.

cognitive_models.situation: The pharmacist points out that a stroke could cause paralysis, directly threatening his physical capabilities and future retirement plans.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: I don't wanna be crippled by a stroke or a heart attack. Taking the medicine sounds like the end of the game right now.
cognitive_models.behavior: Committing to the medication regimen to prevent physical impairment.
